newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Challenger swings ahead in Gambia poll.
newsitem.headline: Challenger swings ahead in Gambia poll.

text.p: The main civilian challenger overtook Gambia's military strongman Yahya Jammeh after three constituencies were declared on Friday from the West African country's presidential election.
The latest official results announced live on television showed chief opposition leader Ousainou Darboe had polled a total of 4,293 ballots, against Jammeh's 3,995.
Darboe outpolled Jammeh by 1,183 ballots in the latest constituency declared -- Keang East in the interior.
Jammeh had polled 556 votes or 54 percent of ballots cast in the first constituency to be declared in Janjanbureh. Darboe polled 423 votes or 41 percent.
Janjanbureh was also the first constituency to be declared in last month's national referendum when Jammeh won a 38 percent "Yes" vote countrywide for a new constitution.

Two other civilian candidates, hotel manager Amath Bah of the National Reconciliation Party (NRP) and Sidia Jatta of the small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism, were trailing far behind Jammeh and Darboe and were generally seen as marginal in the election.

Final results were expected late on Friday with a close race forecast between Jammeh and Darboe, who is leader of the United Democratic Party. Jammeh is a candidate of the Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction.
